name: looks
about: Does the design look like its reference? Adapted from 3dcodeverse's reference and static_object rubrics (github.com/gaoypeng/3dcodeverse, Apache-2.0) for a 3D-printed robot judged at N1 or N2.
pass_threshold_why: 0.70 is the rubric's own «clearly the same robot» anchor.
extra_instructions: Images labelled REFERENCE are the target; images labelled VIEW are renders of the design. Compare like with like: the render view closest to the reference's viewpoint against the reference. Judge the FORM only: the renders are flat shaded (grey or a few flat colours) and the robot will be printed in PLA of colours chosen later, so colour, lighting, background, the hand holding the model and camera framing are never faults. At N1 and N2 the real parts' shape counts. The gate facts and measured numbers are computed by code: use them, never re-estimate them. CALIBRATION: 0.9+ = a stranger shown the render next to the reference says it is the same robot, every visible part present and in proportion; 0.7 = clearly the same robot, one proportion or part visibly off; 0.5 = recognisably the same kind of robot, but a major proportion or part is wrong; 0.2 = a different robot. A design that matches the reference in silhouette but is missing a part the reference shows must lose on parts_coverage, not be rescued by proportions. The defect checklist is binary and literal: present only when an image or a gate finding shows it, and cite it.

criteria.title: Silhouette match (measured)
criteria.description: Outline IoU of the render against the reference's silhouette mask, computed by code. Dropped when no mask exists.

criteria.title: Proportions vs reference
criteria.description: Overall aspect (width : length : height), the body's height over the ground, the body against the legs' span, the size and spacing of repeated parts (legs, eyes).

anchors.1.0: Every ratio matches the reference within a few percent.
anchors.0.7: One ratio visibly off (body a little tall, legs a little short), still reads as the reference.
anchors.0.4: A clearly wrong ratio changes the character (a tall box on stilts where the reference is a low dome).

criteria.title: Parts coverage
criteria.description: Is every part the reference shows present, counted right and placed as there (shell, face, eyes, legs, underbody), and nothing invented that changes the look?

anchors.1.0: Every visible reference part present, right count, right place; nothing invented.
anchors.0.7: One minor part missing or simplified (a small eye, a panel).
anchors.0.4: A major part missing or miscounted, or an invented part that changes the look.

criteria.title: Stance and legs
criteria.description: How the robot stands: leg count, how far they spread, the knee height against the body, the leg segments' shape and taper, the feet on the ground.

anchors.1.0: Legs read exactly as the reference's: count, spread, knee height, segment shape.
anchors.0.7: Right count and stance; segment shape or knee height a little off.
anchors.0.4: Legs clearly different (too straight, too short, wrong spread).
anchors.0.1: Legs unlike the reference's or missing.

criteria.title: Detail fidelity
criteria.description: The reference's visible details (panel lines, eye rims, the shell's ridges, the leg joints) reproduced as shape.

anchors.1.0: Nearly every reference detail exists as modelled shape.
anchors.0.7: Major details present, fine ones smoothed.
anchors.0.1: A primitive approximation where the level asks for real parts.

criteria.title: Cleanliness
criteria.description: No artefacts: holes, inverted faces, slivers, floating fragments, parts through each other.

defects.text: The renders show a different robot than the reference (or nothing recognisable).
A major part the reference shows (a leg, the face, the eyes, the shell) is absent from every view.
A part visibly hovers or is detached from the rest (daylight between it and its support).
A part visibly passes through another (a leg through the shell), or a gate FAIL reports a collision.
The back, a side or the underside is missing or open where the reference is closed.
Missing faces, see-through walls or black inverted faces are visible.
